about:
Custom Wire Industries, Inc. has operated from Muskego, Wisconsin since its founding in 1968. The company began as a manufacturer of electrical wire and cable assemblies and has since expanded into a range of electromechanical fabrication services.

The company produces custom wire harnesses, cable assemblies, ribbon cables, overmolded components, lead wires, electromechanical devices, kits, control panels, and power transmission assemblies. Its capabilities include cable fabrication, wire harness assembly, electromechanical assembly, custom tooling, injection molding, overmolding, CAD-based design, and turnkey kitted assemblies. Custom Wire Industries handles projects from microscopic components to 900-pound alert tower assemblies.

Customers span medical, military, industrial, telecommunications, and automotive sectors. The firm fabricates cables for medical equipment, military-spec power cable systems, industrial machinery, and automotive wire harnesses.

Custom Wire Industries emphasizes affordable pricing, fast turnaround times, and a 100% quality management system with strict quality control at each manufacturing stage. All components meet or exceed UL and CSA regulations. The company also offers design services, allowing clients to consolidate components and reduce shipping and labor costs.

name: Cutlist CO
old_description: Precision CNC ROUTING AND LASER CUTTING for ARTISTS, MAKERS, BUILDERS AND DESIGNERS.
about:
Cutlist CO operates a digital fabrication studio in Denver, Colorado, founded in 2006. The company provides CNC routing and laser cutting services to artists, makers, builders, and designers from its Colorado facility.

The shop runs a ShopSabre CNC router equipped with a 12-position automatic tool changer and vacuum hold-down, alongside a pro-series laser cutter and 3D printing capabilities. It processes full 48-by-96-inch sheets of plywood, plastic, and composite materials, delivering 2D profiles, dados, pockets, drill patterns, and laser engraving. Batch production runs of 500 identical parts are routine, and nested sheet optimization reduces waste. Most jobs ship within 10 business days.

Customers range from individual artists creating installation components to small businesses needing 200 identical product parts. The studio serves interior designers building statement pieces, furniture makers producing cabinets and shelving, prototypers developing models and jigs, and retailers requiring signage and display shelving. Materials include Baltic birch, maple, MDF, acrylic, PVC, ABS, foam, cardboard, fabric, and leather.

Cutlist CO distinguishes itself by focusing strictly on cutting—no assembly, finishing, or design work—so clients receive precision parts ready for their own processes. The company sources its own sheet stock to guarantee flatness and machine compatibility, and it maintains a $500 job minimum for CNC routing. The founders built the business on the premise that if you can design it, you should be able to build it locally.

Its product lines include three-phase and single-phase pad-mount transformers, overhead transformers, dry-type transformers, power transformers, auto reclosers, switchgear, breakers, switches, and accessories. about:
D.W. Woodcraft, Inc. was founded in 1983 by David and Julie Rust Posey in Ava, Missouri.

The company specializes in custom woodworking, producing kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, entertainment centers, bookshelves, desks, armoires, and other built-in furniture. In 1990 Posey adopted a computer-aided design and estimating system that generates cut lists for cabinet components. The operation moved to a larger facility on Highway 5 South in 1992–1993, where at its peak the shop employed nine craftsmen. Today the firm operates a showroom on Shull Street where clients can view materials and discuss projects.

D.W. Woodcraft serves residential homeowners, builders, and remodelers in the Ava, Missouri area and surrounding communities. Projects range from full kitchen remodels with features such as lazy susans, custom islands with overhead storage, and integrated pantries, to bathroom vanities with double sinks and decorative wooden tub surrounds. The company also creates freestanding entertainment centers, bookshelves, and custom furniture pieces for residential spaces.

The Poseys started the business to bring personalized, handcrafted cabinetry to local homes, emphasizing direct collaboration with clients to achieve a "wow factor" in each piece. The company highlights its design-to-build approach, free estimates, and a showroom that allows customers to select materials in person.

Delaney Manufacturing Services LLC has operated from Bradenton, Florida since 1976. The company provides plastic injection molding and full-service product development, offering capabilities that span CAD design, prototyping, tooling, production, assembly, and packaging under one roof.

The shop runs plastic injection molding for volumes ranging from a single piece to millions of parts, with no minimum or maximum order requirements. Services include 3D printing for rapid prototypes, renderings and animations for design validation, and metal-to-plastic conversion programs that replace machined components with engineered resins. All work is performed in-house at the Bradenton facility.

Customers come from consumer goods, medical, military, and industrial sectors, as well as other manufacturers needing component production. The company also works directly with inventors and entrepreneurs to develop new products from concept through retail-ready packaging and drop shipping.

Delaney Manufacturing differentiates itself by consolidating every step — CAD, mold making, molding, assembly, packaging, and logistics — in a single location. It promises same-business-day quote responses, provides a downloadable NDA, and imposes no order minimums, aiming to reduce lead times and simplify supply chains for both established manufacturers and first-time product developers.

The company also serves oilfield companies, electrical contractors, mining operations, and welding shops that require FR protective gear. Individual buyers, including first responders and recreational users, can purchase hats, boots, gloves, coveralls, uniforms, underwear, and individual equipment directly.

Founded by veterans, Dakota Outerwear emphasizes delivering reliable, durable protective gear at competitive prices. The company highlights its ability to source hard-to-find clothing items for specialized military and police applications and its commitment to integrating new fabric technologies to enhance performance in extreme conditions.

about:
Fairfield Manufacturing operates from Lafayette, Indiana, where it was founded in 1919. A satellite plant in Belgaum, India, extends its reach to global customers.

The plant produces custom gears and complete drive systems, handling every step from engineering and design through machining, heat treatment, assembly, and inspection. The company supplies components such as Spicer Torque-Hub track drives and large carrier assemblies forged to unique material specifications.

Fairfield emphasizes its in-house integration of design, manufacturing, testing, and certification as a differentiator, citing gear quality to AGMA Class 14, a global parts and service network, and recent investments in automated assembly driven by a manufacturing execution system that nearly tripled output of certain track drives within the existing footprint.

about:
Daniels Manufacturing Corporation (DMC) was founded in 1947 by Bill Daniels in Pontiac, Michigan, and incorporated in 1949 in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan. The company established its headquarters in Orlando, Florida, in 1984 following a merger with Balmar. DMC is a veteran-owned small business that emphasizes a family culture and has been producing tooling for mission-critical electrical systems for over 75 years.

DMC designs and manufactures precision crimp tools, tool kits, connector assembly tools, Safe-T-Cable® systems, wire preparation tools, and LaceLok® wire harness supports. The company also provides custom tooling solutions, taking projects from concept through design, testing, and manufacturing in its Orlando facility, which houses CNC milling and turning machines, EDM equipment, dual-axis CNC live tooling, and precision grinders. Many of its tools are listed on the Department of Defense Qualified Products List (QPL) and are manufactured in the United States.

DMC serves a broad range of industries, including government (ground, naval, aviation, space), aviation (OEM, MRO, eVTOL, rotorcraft, commercial and executive airlines, drones), space (satellites, launch vehicles, space station), medical (devices and equipment), telecommunications (military and hardened networks, RF wireless), automotive (OEM, service/repair, motorsport, off-highway), rail (wayside, locomotive), power generation (hydro, solar, wind, natural gas, nuclear), and automation (mining, manufacturing, robotics).

The company differentiates itself through a nationwide team of tooling experts who visit customer facilities, active participation in industry standards associations, and a commitment to custom solutions built in-house. DMC’s quality management system is certified to AS9100D and ISO 9001:2015 by NSF-ISR, and its veteran-owned, small-business status underscores a focus on precision, dependability, and long-term customer relationships.

name: Dapwood Furniture Co.
old_description: since 1985. Our 30 years experience makes us the favorite choice of Organic and Natural Mattress Stores throughout the United States and Canada.
about:
Dapwood Furniture Co. was founded in 1985 in Albuquerque, New Mexico. The company operates as a Certified B Corporation and holds New Mexico True certification, reflecting its commitment to social and environmental standards.

The workshop produces solid wood platform bed frames, tables, nightstands, and other bedroom furniture. Each piece is handcrafted from U.S.-grown walnut, cherry, hard maple, and oak, using traditional joinery—cutting, planing, routing, drilling, and fitting—without automated equipment. Products are made to order, offering over 21 million design combinations, and can be left unfinished or finished with natural oils and plant-based stains free of heavy metals and petrochemicals. The facility runs on renewable energy and recycles waste, earning the New Mexico Small Business Recycler Award and a Silver Level Green Zia award.

Dapwood’s primary wholesale customers are organic and natural mattress stores across the United States and Canada. The company also sells directly to consumers in urban markets such as Denver, New York, Portland, Seattle, and Washington, D.C., positioning its furniture as a healthy complement to organic mattresses.

The business was built on a philosophy of avoiding imported composite furniture that relies on adhesives, fumigation, and toxic finishes. By using only solid wood, non-toxic finishes, and American labor, Dapwood aims to provide durable, repairable products that keep chemicals out of the bedroom and reduce landfill waste, backed by a 10-year warranty and replaceable parts.

about:
Design Distillery operates a modern furniture showroom and design studio in Baltimore, Maryland. The company was founded in 1998 by Karen Graveline, who began with a search for vintage modern furniture to furnish her Baltimore rowhome. That pursuit evolved from a small storefront on Charles Street into a 9,000-square-foot showroom near the Inner Harbor.

The firm curates collections from international brands such as Eilersen, Ethnicraft, Trica Furniture, Calligaris, Thayer Coggin, and American Leather. Beyond retail, Design Distillery provides interior design services, including space planning, furniture specification, and custom piece development. The showroom serves as a collaborative environment where clients and fellow designers can test furniture and explore materials.

The client base spans residential homeowners and commercial projects, with the team drawing on Graveline’s background in commercial interior design and marketing. Designers Erin Friedel and Graveline work directly with clients and trade professionals to create tailored interiors.

Graveline credits her architect father for instilling an appreciation for design’s impact on daily life. The company’s stated mission is to offer quality in everything it does, from supplier selection to design execution, driven by a passion for crafting original interiors.

name: Design Molded Plastics
old_description: Design Molded Plastics is a leading provider of mold design and manufacturing solutions, serving a wide range of industries.
about:
Design Molded Plastics operates from Macedonia, Ohio. The company has been in business for over three decades, specializing in custom plastic injection molding. No founding year or founders are disclosed, and ownership details are not publicly stated.

The company provides mold design, plastic injection molding (including two-shot, in-mold labeling, scientific, high-heat, and vertical molding), decorating via hot stamping, assembly, warehousing and logistics, engineering, and design and development. Its press capabilities range from 88 to 950 tons, with rotary two-shot machines up to 500 tons and a 220-ton vertical molding machine with a rotary table. RJG-certified master molders lead the process engineering team. Facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Design Molded Plastics serves the automotive, healthcare, sports and recreation, appliances, and safety industries. It also supports metal-to-plastic conversion projects across various sectors.

The company differentiates itself through scientific molding practices, high-heat molding up to 390°F for advanced resins such as PEEK and carbon-filled PEEK, two-shot and overmolding expertise, and a quality system registered to ISO 9001:2015 with APQP/PPAP processes. Advanced inspection equipment includes Zeiss CMMs, optical measurement systems, and SPC workstations.

name: DiLanna Foodservice and Paper Products
old_description: Family owned since 1939, DiLanna Foodservice and Paper Products has spent more than eight decades helping local establishments with all their foodservice and supply needs.
about:
DiLanna Foodservice and Paper Products operates from Johnston, Rhode Island, where it was founded in 1939 as a family-owned business. Now in its fourth generation, the company continues under the leadership of David DiLanna, who has maintained a practice of hiring local residents and preserving the family-oriented approach that defined its early years.

The company distributes a broad range of foodservice and paper products, including canned and dry goods, meat and poultry, dairy and frozen items, paper products and packaging, convenience foods, grocery staples, and specialty seasonal items. Its catalog expands daily, and orders are fulfilled through direct delivery across Rhode Island and into southeastern Massachusetts, supported by a mobile app that provides access to personalized order guides.

DiLanna serves restaurants and full-service dining establishments, pizzerias, convenience stores, grocery stores, nursing homes and healthcare facilities, and other institutional accounts. The customer base spans neighborhood eateries in Providence to large institutional operations on the South Shore.

The business emphasizes personal service and reliability, with a team led by industry veterans such as Director of Sales Anthony Melillo, who brings more than 30 years of hands-on experience from dishwasher to chef and food-and-beverage manager. The company positions its differentiator as answering the phone personally, delivering dependably, and treating customers like family.

Diagnostic Medical Equipment Inc. was founded in 2011 in Moore, Oklahoma. The company is led by CEO Arun Mirchia and operates from a facility on Messenger Lane. With over 15 years of expertise in healthcare, the firm has built a reputation for mutual service and efficient delivery.

Its client base spans globally, with a focus on healthcare institutions requiring advanced ultrasound technology. The company states its core values are mutual service and efficient delivery, aiming to create stable transactions that benefit global healthcare sectors. It emphasizes constantly updating inventory to meet changing market demands and provides crating and shipping as part of every purchase.

DiaMed, Inc. is based in Windham, Maine, and has specialized in antibody products since its founding in 1983. Founded in 1983, the company has maintained a narrow focus on antibody technologies, building a service portfolio that spans from early-stage research support to larger-scale production.

The company provides contract antibody services including purification, conjugation, and modification tailored to customer specifications. It operates at scales ranging from research-size batches to bulk production, and also offers custom buffer formulation and concentration adjustment. DiaMed also sells excess conjugated antibody material from previous runs at reduced cost, and assists clients during product development by manufacturing research-scale batches of purified, labeled, and modified antibodies. The firm notes that its services can be scaled in accordance with client needs, whether for bulk amounts or research-scale batches.

The company serves organizations engaged in antibody-based research and product development, providing research-scale manufacturing support for purified, labeled, and modified antibodies. It also supplies excess conjugated antibody inventory to buyers seeking cost-effective reagents. DiaMed's customer base includes those developing new products who require assistance during the development process.

DiaMed highlights its scalable service model, its ability to adjust final product concentration and buffer systems to client requirements, and its focus on antibody-specific expertise developed over decades. The company states that it has specialized in antibody products since 1983, emphasizing its long-standing experience in the field.

name: Diamond Electric Mfg. Corp
old_description: We deliver fantastic products and are committed to quality through dedicated teamwork.
about:
Diamond Electric Mfg. Corp. traces its roots to 1937, when Inosuke Tomita founded Diamond Electric in Japan. The company established its U.S. presence in 1990 with Diamond Electric United States (DEUS) in Dundee, Michigan, led by first president Nobu Hashimoto. In 1996, ground broke on a new plant in Eleanor, West Virginia, where mass production of ignition coils began in 1997. The Eleanor facility held its grand opening in 1998 and has since expanded multiple times. Today the corporate office remains in Eleanor, while a sales and design center operates in Farmington Hills, Michigan, near Detroit’s automotive hub.

The company designs, manufactures, and distributes automotive electrical components, specializing in ignition coils. Its capabilities span design engineering, research and development, manufacturing, and thorough product testing. Multiple U.S. locations provide manufacturing, sales, and support for global OEM customers. The Eleanor plant handles high-volume coil production, while the Farmington Hills center focuses on design and customer collaboration.

Diamond Electric serves three primary customer groups: OEM automotive manufacturers, service-part retailers, and DIY installers. It has earned quality awards from major automakers, including a President’s Product Quality Award from Subaru of Indiana Automotive in 2004. The company also supports community initiatives in Putnam County, West Virginia, where it was named Corporate Citizen of the Year in 2005.

The business is guided by a philosophy that prioritizes trust, superb quality, and the happiness of all stakeholders. Core values include customer focus, community involvement, integrity, teamwork, open communication, and safety. Diamond Electric emphasizes partnering with stakeholders as the key to the future, delivering products on time and defect-free through dedicated teamwork and constant improvement.

old_description: Custom fabrication of spiral duct, flat oval duct, and precision fittings.
about:
Diaz Sheet Metal, LLC was established in 2005 in Hyattsville, Maryland. The company operates as a licensed and insured mechanical contractor specializing in sheet metal fabrication, HVAC systems, and plumbing services for commercial and residential clients across the state.

The shop produces custom spiral duct, flat oval duct, and precision fittings using CNC plasma cutting and automated coil lines, working with galvanized steel, black iron, 304/316 stainless steel, and aluminum. Full 3D CAD modeling and shop drawing services feed directly into fabrication, ensuring compliance with SMACNA standards and a tolerance of ±0.01 inch. Beyond fabrication, the firm installs and maintains rooftop units, VAV systems, split systems, heat pumps, boilers, and ductless mini-splits, and provides plumbing services including drain cleaning, repiping, sewer repair, and hydro jetting.

Customers include Maryland contractors, facility managers, and homeowners. Project examples range from commercial HVAC system installations and industrial ventilation upgrades to custom spiral ductwork for commercial layouts, main sewer repairs, and cooling tower servicing. The company partners with Trane and Carrier for equipment supply.

The company emphasizes a rapid response guarantee with a sub-two-hour reaction time for critical failures, a zero-defect policy, and BIM coordination to resolve field conflicts before installation. Its stated goal is to provide the gold standard of technical service to the local community with absolute precision and rapid response.

name: Digitron Semiconductors
old_description: The military quality level is designed for customers whose applications require the parts to be fully robust and reliable in military applications
about:
Digitron Semiconductors operates from Kenilworth, New Jersey, where it manufactures high-reliability discrete semiconductor devices. The company focuses on Zener diodes, transient voltage suppressors, rectifiers, and transistors tailored to stringent military, aerospace, industrial, and commercial requirements.

The product portfolio spans thousands of part numbers across categories such as TVS devices (2 W to 100,000 W), bridge rectifiers (2 A to 35 A), Zener diodes (250 mW to 100 W), and various transistor types including BJTs, JFETs, MOSFETs, SCRs, and triacs. Digitron emphasizes a high-mix, low-to-mid-volume production model with reasonable lead times and an internal test laboratory capable of MIL-PRF-19500 JANTX-equivalent screening, environmental stress testing (temperature cycling, burn-in), and customized test flows. All quality levels receive lot-based test reports and certificates of compliance.

Customers include defense and aerospace contractors, industrial equipment manufacturers, and commercial electronics producers. The military/aerospace grade meets full robustness for harsh environments, the industrial grade offers extended temperature operation and higher endurance, while the commercial grade undergoes four levels of 100% inspection achieving a 0.99998 assurance level for less stressful applications.

Digitron positions itself as a risk-mitigating supplier by combining broad product availability, stable year-over-year pricing, and a quality system registered to AS9100:2016 and ISO 9001:2015. Its quality policy targets on-time delivery and continuous improvement on every order, supported by source-control drawing accommodation and in-house delta and PDA calculations.

name: Direct Wire (Direct Wire & Cable)
old_description: Direct Wire is a leading manufacturer of industry-best wire and cable systems and assemblies
about:
Direct Wire, based in Denver, Pennsylvania, was founded in 1977 as a small business operating from a home garage in Pennsylvania. The company has grown into a profitable U.S.-based manufacturer of wire and cable systems and assemblies, maintaining a commitment to domestic production and ethical, sustainable operations.

The company manufactures a broad portfolio of wire and cable products under flagship brands such as Flex-A-Prene®, Ultra-Flex®, All-Flex®, Veri-Flex®, and Dura-Flex®, serving welding, power, industrial, data center, renewable energy, battery, and entertainment applications. Direct Wire also produces oxygen-free copper rod and stems in 8 mm and 12.5 mm diameters at its Lancaster facility. In-house capabilities include cable assembly, proprietary compound coloring, longitudinal stripe extrusion (pioneered in 2000), inkjet and indent printing, a repair and spark-testing program, copper recycling, private labeling, and same‑ or next‑day fulfillment from distribution warehouses in Denver and Lancaster.

Direct Wire serves industries including renewable energy (solar, wind, EV charging, battery storage), industrial and OEM, power and renewables, data centers, welding, battery and motive power, entertainment and stage lighting, vehicle and transit, oil, gas, and mining, distribution, rental equipment, and appliance and electronics. Customers cited include Michigan CAT, IWS Gas and Supply, and ILMO Products Company.

The company emphasizes its U.S.-based manufacturing heritage as a differentiator, citing shorter lead times, job creation, and higher quality. Its “Service. Technology. People.” philosophy is backed by an on-site quality laboratory that conducts testing to UL, ASTM, SAE, and MSHA standards, and by proprietary rubber and plastic compounds engineered for durability.

The company was established in 1993 and has served the region's sheet metal needs for over three decades.

The shop specializes in custom sheet metal fabrication, cutting and bending galvanized steel to produce HVAC ductwork, plenums, transitions, fittings, and a range of one-off parts such as brackets, signs, panels, and covers. It accepts orders from a single piece to production quantities, working from customer drawings, photos, samples, or even rough field sketches. The team also offers field measurement services to verify dimensions before fabrication. Finished parts are typically ready for quick pickup.

Primary customers include HVAC and mechanical contractors who encounter field conditions that don't match catalog parts, as well as homeowners needing replacement duct fittings or transitions. The company also supports retrofit projects and small-run custom metalwork for a variety of industrial and commercial applications.

Diversified Metal Fabricators distinguishes itself by accepting virtually any form of part definition — from formal prints to marked-up photos — and by delivering fabricated assemblies with mechanical joints that eliminate exposed fasteners. The emphasis on rapid turnaround for pickup and the ability to scope parts in a single conversation are cited as key advantages.

With more than 60 employees, the facility runs injection molding machines with shot capacities from 19 to 311 ounces, four 80,000‑pound material silos, and a broad CNC lineup that includes HAAS machining centers. Diversified Plastics delivers tens of thousands of parts annually, from prototype quantities to production runs of thousands.

Customers span lumber and pulp processing, industrial wastewater treatment, mining, forest products, oil‑field equipment (such as McClain Oil Tools), grain handling, car‑wash systems, and even local breweries. The company ships to over 15 countries and serves OEMs, maintenance departments, and distributors seeking metal‑to‑plastic conversions, wear‑resistant components, and complex assemblies.

Diversified Plastics differentiates itself through its MultiFab approach, which integrates fabrication, machining, injection molding, and polyurethane casting to reduce lead times and enable single‑source sourcing. Lean production protocols and collaborative, on‑site problem solving have been core to the operation since its garage start.

name: EPECOMPONENTS / ELECTRONIC PARTS EXCHANGE
old_description: EPE helps OEMs, EMS providers, and global supply chains recover value from excess, obsolete, and slow-moving electronic components through transparent resale and inventory recovery programs.
about:
EPE Components operates from Salem, Massachusetts, where it serves as a specialized intermediary for excess and obsolete electronic inventory. The company focuses on helping original equipment manufacturers, electronics manufacturing services providers, and global supply chains convert idle component stock into working capital through structured resale and recovery programs.

Its service lines include excess inventory recovery via consignment or buyout, secure authorized remarketing to protect brand integrity, ESG circular reporting with data-backed sustainability metrics, and lifecycle obsolescence management to maintain supply continuity. Quality assurance is anchored by an AS9120B:2016 and ISO 9001:2015 certified management system, supplemented by ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 certifications. Inspection and testing capabilities cover documentation review, packaging verification, external visual inspection, remarking and resurfacing tests (scrape and solvent), X-ray inspection using an X6600/X6600B microfocus system, solderability testing on a MUST System 3 platform, decapsulation via a JetEtch chemical system, and high-magnification microscopy on a Keyence instrument (20–6000×). The company also maintains AS6081 compliance for counterfeit detection.

EPE's customer base spans automotive, aviation/military, and medical sectors. In automotive, commodity managers monitor lead-time and obsolescence issues for components from suppliers such as NVIDIA, Intel, NXP, Infineon, Texas Instruments, Renesas, Bosch, Onsemi, and STMicroelectronics. Aviation and military clients rely on the firm's AS9120 certification and use of DOD-certified test facilities when required. Medical customers receive semiconductors and LCDs sourced through a strict vendor screening process.

The company emphasizes transparent recovery processes, global buyer access to maximize pricing, and consignment strategies that it says often outperform traditional liquidation. Its quality program is built around rigorous incoming and outgoing inspection, detailed test reporting, and traceability documentation.

about:
Eaton Sales & Service LLC traces its origins to 1919 in Casper, Wyoming. The business evolved from Eaton Metal Products Company, which was active in petroleum equipment during the 1950s before financial pressures in the 1960s shifted its focus to tank and steel fabrication. In the early 1980s, the company re-entered the petroleum equipment market through a series of acquisitions and internal growth, formally adopting the Eaton Sales & Service LLC name by the mid-1990s.

Today the company manufactures above-ground and underground fuel storage tanks and provides full-spectrum petroleum equipment sales, installation, and service across nine locations in Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, New Mexico, and Arizona. Its capabilities span fueling system construction, lubrication equipment service, mechanical integrity inspection, and distribution. The firm maintains a team of factory- and regulatory-certified technicians trained on brands such as Wayne, Veeder Root, OPW, Franklin, Verifone, Rotary, Graco, and Champion, and reports more than 500,000 completed projects and 30,000 active customers.

Eaton serves retail and commercial fueling stations, agricultural operations, marinas, and aviation facilities. Its customer base includes major oil companies, big-box retailers, grocery chains, and independent fueling operators throughout the Rocky Mountain region.

The company states its mission is to anticipate and exceed customer expectations with responsive, cost-effective manufacturing, construction, and service. It emphasizes safety, quality, and innovation, citing unmatched buying power from century-long manufacturer relationships and an engineering team that supports its tank designs.

name: EcoGen America
old_description: Founded in 2016, we have expanded from regional roots to a nationwide data-driven platform, accumulating nearly a decade of direct solar industry exposure.
about:
EcoGen America is based in Camden, Delaware, and was founded in 2016 by Trevor Guilday to connect homeowners with local solar installers. The company expanded nationwide in 2022 to cover all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico, and rebuilt its platform in 2025 with a homeowner-first brand and stricter verification frameworks. Chief Executive Officer Dean Mahmoud, who has worked in residential solar since 2021, leads the business alongside Guilday, who maintains the company's Solar Cost Index.

The firm operates an independent solar education platform that publishes state-level cost benchmarks, incentive explanations, and savings calculators. Its proprietary EcoGen Solar Database combines government and laboratory data — including benchmarks from the Department of Energy's National Laboratory of the Rockies, wage data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, and electricity-use figures from the Energy Information Administration — with a calibrated cost model and marketplace quote data. As of September 2026, the platform listed six verified installer partners and had processed more than 25,000 quote requests.

EcoGen serves residential homeowners across the United States who are evaluating solar installations. The service is free to users; the company earns referral fees from partner installers but states that compensation does not influence editorial content. Installers that pass three published checks — an active state license, documented installations in the state, and a workmanship warranty covering roof penetrations — receive an EcoGen Verified Installer badge.

The platform was created to address a transparency gap in the solar industry, where homeowners faced high-pressure sales tactics without reliable data. The company emphasizes editorial independence, public data sourcing, and partner accountability through complaint review and TCPA compliance agreements.

Ecotex serves healthcare systems across Canada and the United States, counting hundreds of hospital locations among its customers. Its client base includes acute-care hospitals, long-term care facilities, and other medical institutions that rely on certified, sustainable linen programs.

The company emphasizes that its family ownership allows rapid decision-making, long-term reinvestment, and direct issue resolution. Ecotex differentiates itself through its Smarter Linen Solutions™ framework, Hygienically Clean and Clean Green certifications, HLAC accreditation, and a stated goal of turning customers into “raving fans” through attentive service and technical excellence.

The firm designs and installs residential and commercial photovoltaic systems, custom battery storage, and backup power solutions, including Tesla Powerwall and Enphase-based installations. It also provides licensed electrical services for residential, commercial, and industrial projects. With an in-house team of 55 employees, Elemental Energy has completed over 4,000 installations totaling 50 megawatts of capacity across Oregon and southern Washington.

Its customers range from homeowners seeking energy independence and off-grid living to businesses pursuing long-term energy cost savings. The company also serves mobile and remote applications, and partners with the nonprofit Twende Solar to deliver renewable energy to communities in South America, Central America, Africa, and Asia.

Elemental Energy differentiates itself through direct employment of all installers, a 10-year workmanship warranty, and certifications such as NABCEP Certified Installer and Technical Sales Professional, Tesla Powerwall Certified Installer, and Enphase Premium Installer. Its humanitarian outlook and focus on education underpin every project.

about:
Elevaris Medical Devices is headquartered in Wilmington, Massachusetts. The company was founded in 1995 as Spectra Medical Devices. Following the acquisition of UK-based XL Precision Technologies, the company rebranded to Elevaris Medical Devices.

The company designs, develops, and manufactures procedural needles, precision micro-components, complex tubular components, and sub-assemblies for the medical device industry. It also distributes pharmaceutical products, surgical instruments, and medical supplies. Manufacturing capabilities include laser technology (4-axis tube laser cutting, flat-bed micro-laser cutting, micro-laser welding, laser marking, laser ablation), micro-machining (EDM wire/sink erosion, 5-axis CNC machining, 3D metal printing), grinding (centerless, CNC, electrochemical, various needle tip geometries), injection molding, insert molding, cleanroom assembly (ISO Class 7 and 8), precision forming (swaging, bending, pressing), and metal finishing (electropolishing, chemical etching, passivation, siliconization, chrome plating). The company operates facilities in the US, UK, and South Korea.

Elevaris serves multinational healthcare companies, global original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), and emerging technology companies in the medical device sector. Customers include medical device companies, spin-offs, and start-ups seeking design, development, and contract manufacturing services.

The company emphasizes its legacy of engineering expertise combined with state-of-the-art equipment, facilities, and processes to deliver high-quality, cost-effective manufacturing. It differentiates itself through a proprietary combination of laser, EDM, 5-axis CNC, and 3D metal printing technologies, cleanroom assembly, fully validated packaging processes (including MULTIVAC systems), and a commitment to ESG values.

Emcee Electronics Inc is based in Venice, Florida, where it designs and manufactures instruments for measuring the electrical conductivity, water separability, and filterability of explosive liquids.

The firm's product line consists of precision test instruments that conform to ASTM International standards, including methods D8073, D3948, and D7224, as well as standards from the Energy Institute (formerly the Institute of Petroleum) and ISO. Emcee Electronics provides technical support, training videos, and instruction manuals for its equipment.

The instruments serve customers in aviation fuel testing and petroleum product testing, where water separation and conductivity measurements are critical for flight safety and fuel quality. The company sells through a dealer network and has partnered with PAC to expand its global reach.

Emcee Electronics emphasizes that its products are 100% American made and produced under an ISO 9001:2015 quality management system. The company has published technical analysis arguing that certain ASTM test methods do not reflect real-world coalescing performance, underscoring its focus on test-method validity.

name: EnaChip Inc.
old_description: In 2013 he returned to Penn to become the Alfred Fitler Moore Professor and Director of Penn’s Singh Center for Nanotechnology. In 2024 he became Chair of Penn’s Department of Electrical and Systems Engineering. Mark’s research is in the area of microelectromechanical systems (MEMS). Beginning with a plenary address to the 1994 IEEE Applied Power Engineering Conference on the topic of integrated inductors, and continuing through today, a major thrust of his program is the realization of microfabricated magnetics for advanced power delivery. He has chaired or co-chaired multiple conferences and co-founded multiple MEMS companies.
about:
EnaChip Inc. operates from Rocky Hill, New Jersey, where it develops high-frequency magnetic components for vertical power delivery in AI data centers.

The company designs and fabricates bespoke magnetics that enable integrated voltage regulator (IVR) and transverse inductor voltage regulator (TLVR) topologies. Its core technology relies on an electroplated core stack with thick copper planar windings and high-flux-density magnetic materials, all processed on standard semiconductor equipment. The resulting components achieve low DC and AC resistance, support switching frequencies above 10 MHz, and fit within sub-millimeter, wafer-level packages that can be placed at the board, package, or die level.

Its magnetics are designed to integrate with gallium nitride (GaN) and advanced silicon switches, targeting the last few centimeters of power delivery where conversion losses are highest. The company also lists energy harvesting and energy conversion among its served markets.

EnaChip states that its differentiation lies in co-designing power, signal, sensing, and actuation functions rather than stitching together disconnected parts. By electroplating on standard semiconductor lines, the company says it dramatically reduces manufacturing time while delivering magnetics that suppress core loss at high frequencies, enabling low-inductance designs that drop into any level of the design stack.

about:
Engineered Plastic Components (EPC Manufacturing) is headquartered in Lebanon, Kentucky, and operates a network of 21 manufacturing facilities across the United States, Canada, and Mexico. The company serves as a Tier 1 supplier to automotive OEMs and provides precision-engineered plastic components for appliance, medical device, and consumer product markets.

The company runs injection molding presses ranging from 25 to 4,400 tons, enabling production of small precision parts up to large automotive components. Core processes include two-shot molding, overmolding, insert molding, gas assist, and in-mold decoration. Secondary operations encompass hot stamping, pad printing, heat transfer, silk screening, heat staking, and multiple welding technologies (sonic, spin, vibration, hot plate, ultrasonic, orbital). Facilities also offer painting (1K/2K/waterborne), powder coating, metal stamping, cleanroom manufacturing, leak testing, and full assembly and sub-assembly. The Lebanon, Kentucky plant spans 250,000 square feet and operates 24/7; the Bellevue, Ohio facility covers 192,000 square feet with 71 presses; other sites range from 52,500 to 150,000 square feet.

EPC supplies complex instrument panel assemblies, interior and exterior trim with Class-A finishes, and painted components to major automotive OEMs. For appliance manufacturers, it produces control panels, structural housings, and components with UV stability and heat resistance. Medical device customers receive FDA-compliant cleanroom-molded surgical instrument components and diagnostic equipment housings made from sterilizable materials. Consumer product lines include electronics housings, protective cases, and appliance parts with emphasis on durability and aesthetics.

The company emphasizes its North American footprint, IATF 16949 and ISO 13485 certifications, and in-house metrology (CMM, vision, DSC) as differentiators. It also highlights environmentally conscious manufacturing using recycled materials and sustainable practices, along with a certified minority-owned facility in Osceola, Wisconsin that provides engineering, tooling support, and mold repair.

EverGreen serves agricultural, residential, government and utility, marine, and wood-foundation construction markets. Residential buyers specify Lifewood for decks, framing, and guardrails. Government and utility projects call for fire-retardant and marine-grade plywood, while wood-foundation systems rely on pressure-treated lumber for below-grade durability.

The company states its focus is on delivering durable, cost-effective treated lumber across the Midwest, backed by a commitment to wood-preservation quality and customer service. UL listing is cited as a mark of compliance for its treated products.

The company adopted the Factory Motor Parts name through its participation in the former Chrysler Mopar distribution network of the 1960s, symbolizing partnerships with Ford, General Motors, and other aftermarket suppliers. From a single location, FMP expanded to over 300 locations across 35 states, with significant growth starting in 1993 when it grew from three to 32 locations in five years, entering markets such as Bismarck, Omaha, Phoenix, and Denver.

FMP distributes premium original equipment (OE) and name-brand automotive parts, positioning itself as a total resource for professional automotive repair. Its service portfolio includes dedicated support teams, the FMP Delivers online ordering platform, fleet supply chain solutions with GPS tracking, technical training, and a customer self-service portal. The company also operates specialized programs such as the Professional Brake Program, Battery Programs, a Stocking Program, the FMP Partners Network for independent shops, and the One Stop Parts Source Program.

The distributor serves independent service centers, car and truck dealerships, commercial fleets, wholesale distributors, and retailers. Customer testimonials cite shops such as Christian Brothers Automotive, Tilden Car Care Center, and Colorado Tire & Service as users of FMP's parts and programs. FMP's market coverage spans the Midwest, Mountain States, Southwest, Northeast, North Carolina, and the West Coast including Alaska.

FMP emphasizes its multi-generational family ownership, unmatched parts availability, knowledgeable staff, and a nationwide warranty as key differentiators. The company states its mission is to be a dynamic, ever-adapting partner that meets and exceeds the unique needs of each customer in the automotive aftermarket.

Referrals come from physicians and patients directly seeking CPAP therapy for obstructive sleep apnea.

name: Falcon Plastics
old_description: Falcon Plastics combines five decades of U.S.-based precision molding expertise with strategic manufacturing in Mexico and Asia to support complex, evolving supply chains. From custom components to value-added assembly and full program support, our multi-facility model gives customers flexibility without sacrificing control, quality, or partnership.
about:
Falcon Plastics was founded in 1975 in Brookings, South Dakota, as a family-owned custom plastics molder. From its start molding customer ideas into quality plastic products, the company has grown into a multi-facility operation with plants in South Dakota, Oregon, and Tennessee, supplemented by strategic manufacturing partnerships in Mexico and Asia.

The company specializes in mid-to-high volume custom injection molding, blow molding, tool and mold making, sheet foaming (EVA), and foam-in-place gasketing. Its facilities include temperature-controlled white rooms with HEPA filtration for clean molding, and smart work cells equipped with process monitoring, automated in-line quality testing, and robotic acceptance or rejection systems. Value-added assembly and lean manufacturing principles support cost-effective volume production.

Falcon serves medical device, electronics, consumer product, automotive, business machine, construction, and recreation/sports markets. Customers rely on the molder for precision components that meet strict regulatory standards in medical applications, durable housings for electronics, and high-performance parts for automotive and industrial uses.

The company emphasizes a multi-facility model that provides supply-chain flexibility without sacrificing control or quality. Its stated differentiators include reducing cycle times, optimizing material usage, and maintaining an ISO 9001:2015 certified quality system across all sites, driven by a culture of continuous improvement and on-time delivery.

old_description: At our core, we have a simple mission: to create handcrafted furniture that is both desirable and affordable. We understand the frustration of searching endlessly for the perfect piece, only to find it either out of reach financially or needing more quality. That’s why we have made it our goal to redefine the concept of “affordable furniture” by offering timeless, unique, and durable pieces made from solid wood. Our commitment extends beyond simply providing furniture. We deeply care about our community and have identified a genuine need for high-quality furniture at an accessible price point. about:
Farmhouse Style Furniture operates from White Bear Township, Minnesota. The business traces its start to 2012 when founder James Putnam built a dining table for a friend, sparking demand for his custom woodworking.

The shop produces custom furniture and cabinetry for kitchens, bathrooms, mudrooms, and living rooms. Every piece is handcrafted from solid wood — oak, cherry, maple, or walnut — using traditional joinery such as dovetail, mortise-and-tenon, and tongue-and-groove joints. The workflow follows a four-step collaboration: design consultation, detailed planning, precision handcrafting, and final installation. A showroom on site lets clients review materials and finishes before production begins.

The customer base is residential homeowners seeking made-to-fit pieces. Recent projects cited in reviews include a sewing cabinet, a bathroom vanity, a mudroom hall tree, a pandemic-era homeschooling table and benches that became a permanent dining set, dining chairs delivered ahead of schedule, a hall-tree entry piece, a dining table with bar stools, and bedroom suites with beds, dressers, and hallway storage.

The company states its mission is to redefine affordable furniture by offering timeless, one-of-a-kind pieces built to last. Putnam emphasizes that the business exists to meet a community need for high-quality, accessible craftsmanship, turning each client's vision into a durable, personalized product.

about:
Fashions Unlimited was founded in 1976 by Phil Spector in Baltimore, Maryland, after he spent a decade working for another local manufacturer.

The facility focuses on activewear, intimate apparel, and swimwear constructed from stretch fabrics. Services span product development, pattern making using AccuMark digital software, 3D digital rendering, cutting on a Gerber automatic cutter, and sewing with overlock, coverstitch, flatlock, zig-zag, and single-needle lockstitch machines. Finishing includes tagging, bagging, and bulk shipping, while repair work covers retagging and rebagging. Production minimums start at 200 pieces per style, with a typical initial order of 300 pieces across multiple colors and sizes.

Clients range from startup brands needing full development to established labels supplying their own patterns and materials. The company has produced for recognized national brands, including Miss Daisy Medical, and serves the activewear, intimate-apparel, and swimwear markets. Material sourcing is limited to domestic suppliers.

Spector’s 50-plus years of industry experience and the firm’s status as one of the few remaining onshore cut-and-sew facilities underpin its positioning. The 3D rendering capability—rare among Maryland manufacturers—aims to reduce sample iterations, and the AccuMark system drives fabric efficiency through digital markers.

name: Findlay Food Coatings
old_description: Findlay Food Coatings can design and blend innovative and individualized recipes for you, our customer.
about:
Findlay Food Coatings operates from Caldwell, Idaho, where its state-of-the-art facility was commissioned in January 2015. The U.S. entity was established in 2013 as part of the Findlay Family Group, a fourth-generation family business with over 100 years of history that began as a local bread bakery on the East Coast of New Zealand. In the 1990s the group expanded into manufacturing Panko breadcrumbs, conventional breadcrumbs, and batter coating systems, later building powder blending sites in Idaho to serve the North American market.

The company designs and blends custom food coating recipes, producing premixes, batter washes, pre-dusts, clear coats, flour-based French fry batters, adhesion batters, and tempura batters. Its Caldwell plant runs automated powder blending lines, backed by a secondary site in Nampa, while additional manufacturing facilities in Gisborne, Dunedin, and Auckland, New Zealand, and Bathurst, Australia, support global operations.

Findlay serves the food coatings industry, developing systems to coat substrates ranging from proteins to vegetables, with a focus on French fry applications. Its customer base consists of a select group of food manufacturers that engage the company for new product development and cost-reduction initiatives on existing lines.

The business emphasizes innovation, reliability, and consistency, positioning itself as a partner that delivers on its promises. Customers are drawn to its ability to think outside the box and provide cost-effective, tailored coating solutions backed by a technical team with worldwide expertise.

about:
Finnu Designs was founded in 2014 by Josh Humble in West Fargo, North Dakota. The company began as a woodworking venture but quickly expanded into metal and stone fabrication, driven by Humble's vision to create custom pieces that go beyond standard furniture.

The shop produces custom built-ins, furniture, and home goods using a six-step design process that moves from concept through creative development, planning, building, delivery, and a 30-day follow-up. Projects are fabricated in-house from wood, metal, and stone, with the team handling design, fabrication, installation, and post-installation care.

Finnu serves residential clients, commercial offices, and hospitality venues such as restaurants. Past customers include homeowners seeking unique barn doors or tables, as well as firms like Mosaic Design & Build that collaborate on commercial and residential projects.

The company emphasizes quality craftsmanship, integrity, and uniqueness as core values, stating that its brand is defined by how work is executed rather than what is produced. All pieces are made in North Dakota, and each build includes a care package and follow-up inspection.

old_description: First Solar’s roots run deep in American soil. Born in the Midwest, headquartered in the Southwest, and shipped worldwide, First Solar is an American success story. Driven by a passion for innovation and powered by American ingenuity, First Solar has consistently invested in American manufacturing and American jobs. about:
The parent company traces its origins to the Midwest and now directs global operations from the Southwest, shipping solar modules worldwide while emphasizing domestic production and job creation.

The facility produces the company's Series 6 and Series 7 thin-film photovoltaic modules, which are built on a proprietary cadmium telluride (CdTe) semiconductor process. In addition to module manufacturing, the operation supports a full ecosystem that includes recycling services, post-sales support, and mounting hardware featuring the SpeedSlot system designed to reduce installation time and hardware costs.

The Series 7 TR1 line is marketed as "Made in America, for America," indicating a focus on domestic content requirements and U.S. energy projects.

First Solar differentiates itself through its CdTe thin-film technology, which it says yields a lower carbon footprint, lower water footprint, and faster energy payback than conventional crystalline silicon panels. The company warrants an annual degradation rate of 0.3 percent and offers what it describes as the industry's only cell-cracking warranty, positioning its product as a lower-risk, higher-lifetime-energy option.

name: First State Fabrication
old_description: Custom Fabrications — Platforms, mezzanines, supports, and custom components built to specification.
about:
First State Fabrication operates from Seaford, Delaware, where it has been in business since 1926. The company provides structural and miscellaneous steel fabrication and installation services.

The shop performs custom metal fabrication including stairs, railings, structural steel assemblies, canopies, and custom components such as platforms and mezzanines. Processes cover sheet metal fabrication in carbon steel, stainless steel, and aluminum; press brake forming, shearing, pipe bending, CNC pipe and tube cutting, CNC plasma cutting, punching, and certified welding. The facility houses a 250-ton 12-foot Accurpress press brake, Ercolina angle rolls and pipe benders, Ellis and Marvel saws, a Bend Tech Dragon CNC pipe/tube cutter, a Betenbender 10-foot shear, two Spydercranes (URW295 and URW547), and a Messer MetalMaster 2.0 5x10-foot high-definition plasma table. In-house detailing with BIM and shop fit-up verification support dimensional accuracy.

The company serves contractors, builders, and design teams on commercial and industrial projects. Its work includes ADA-compliant hand and guardrail systems engineered to IBC/ADA standards, architectural steel assemblies, and epoxy-coated components for wastewater and chemical plant environments. Community involvement in Seaford and surrounding towns reflects a local customer base.

First State Fabrication emphasizes schedule-driven delivery, code-ready fabrication, and shop-to-field accuracy. It highlights AWS-certified welders, in-house BIM detailing, pre-shipment mock-ups, and the ability to provide installation with its own crane fleet as factors that distinguish its offering.

name: Fisher Auto Parts
old_description: In 1929, when our country was entering the great depression, Blair Coiner founded his company with high hopes, perseverance and determination.
about:
Fisher Auto Parts traces its roots to 1929 in Weston, West Virginia, where Blair Coiner founded the business during the Great Depression. Originally operating as Coiner Parts, the company began by supplying auto parts to car dealers, service stations, and independent garages.

By 1983 the operation had expanded to 60 locations and 300 employees, prompting a rebrand to Fisher Auto Parts. Today the company runs a network of retail stores and Federated Car Care Centers, distributing name-brand automotive components and offering fast delivery to professional installers. Headcount at the Weston headquarters stands at 18.

Fisher Auto Parts stocks a broad range of replacement parts, appearance chemicals, and detailing supplies sourced from major manufacturers.

The founder’s original mandate — “rendering dealer service of the highest character at all times” — remains the stated differentiator, emphasizing dependable delivery, competitive pricing on quality brands, and a service-first approach for professional buyers.

name: Flair USA
old_description: Vertically integrated for full product development & customer-focused innovation
about:
Founded in 1992 in Appleton, Wisconsin, Flair Packaging (operating as Flair USA) is a privately held, family-owned manufacturer of flexible packaging. The company began as a market-driven operation focused on customer-focused innovation and has grown into a vertically integrated supplier with facilities across North America and Asia.

Flair produces rollstock films, pouches, bags, sustainable packaging, and tactile packaging from its integrated facilities, which include an extrusion plant, converting lines, an analytical laboratory, and an application lab. The company added 10-color flexo printing and solventless lamination at its 35,000-square-foot Calgary plant and operates additional sites in Lacey, Washington; Tlajomulco, Jalisco; Seoul and Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Capabilities span COEX and laminated films, lidding and thermoforming films, vacuum pouches, rotogravure printing, and custom structures engineered for hot-fill, high-pressure processing, and retort applications.

The company serves food and nonfood brands across categories including meat and poultry, seafood, cheese and dairy, prepared foods, snacks and sweets, baby foods, grains and spices, fruits and vegetables, coffee and tea, liquids and spreads, pet care, and foodservice. A stock program offers unprinted, ready-to-label formats such as FlairPak vacuum pouches and rollstock lidding films with lower minimums and faster lead times from strategically located warehouses.

Flair emphasizes collaborative innovation, controlling quality from extrusion through conversion, and holds FSSC 22000 certification (GFSI-recognized) with FDA, USDA, and CFIA compliance. Its ACTIV8 oxygen-absorber sachets and PE mono-material recyclable coffee bags illustrate a focus on shelf-life extension and sustainability.

about:
Flat-To-Form Metal Specialties, Inc. is a sheet metal fabrication shop based in Fremont, Michigan, founded in 1995. The company operates from a facility at 9577 W. 40th Street in Newaygo County and serves manufacturers throughout Michigan and beyond.

The shop provides a range of custom fabrication services including turret punching (24 gauge to 7 gauge), shearing, forming, laser cutting, plasma cutting, tapping, press-in fastener installation, and welding (MIG, TIG, spot, and stud). It also offers assembly of components such as hinges, fasteners, foam gaskets, locks, and clasps, as well as custom prototyping for testing before full production. The company handles jobs from a few punched holes to orders of thousands of assembled pieces.

Its customer base spans diverse manufacturing sectors. Notable clients include Mighty Lube Systematic Lubrication, Inc. in Fremont and OPCO Lubrication Systems, Inc. in West Michigan, both of which rely on Flat-To-Form for complex sheet metal parts requiring punching, forming, welding, and assembly. The company has also produced parts for office furniture and gas pump manufacturers, indicating a broad industrial reach.

Flat-To-Form emphasizes a quality management system certified to ISO 9001:2015, maintained through internal audits, management reviews, and annual surveillance audits. It differentiates itself with in-house prototyping, flexible shipping options including delivery, UPS, FedEx, and freight, and a willingness to provide its quality policy manual upon request.

name: Florida Circuit LLC
old_description: Florida Circuit offers Electronic Component Kitting with complete Bill of Material coverage.
about:
Florida Circuit LLC was established in 2000 in Sunrise, Florida, as a full-service electronic component resource company. The business began by offering kitting solutions and outsourced procurement services to electronic manufacturers seeking to streamline their supply chains.

Florida Metal Works operates from Gulf Breeze, Florida, where it was founded in 2013 by Shane Kahl. A veteran of the U.S. Air Force with seven years of service and multiple deployments, Kahl applied the metal fabrication skills he developed in the military to launch the shop as a veteran-owned business.

The company provides custom metal fabrication and large-scale production runs for both consumer and industrial clients. Its capabilities include CNC 6 kW laser cutting, a 7-axis 150-ton CNC brake, MIG, TIG, and robotic welding, as well as fiber laser engraving for part marking and panel layouts. Work is programmed through CAD software and covers plate and sheet metals, with aluminum frequently used for railings, handrails, brackets, cabinets, and vehicle accessories.

The shop’s own product line includes items such as Sea-Doo fishfinder mounts, Ford Super Duty cowl mounting brackets, tool and battery holders, and aluminum crawfish paddles, while custom projects address specialized brackets, enclosures, and structural components for industrial buyers.

Kahl’s military background drives a focus on precision and deadline adherence, and the company emphasizes close collaboration with clients to translate requirements into finished parts.

name: Food Bank of Delaware
old_description: The Food Bank of Delaware distributes food statewide through a network of partners. Food is easily accessible from local food closets, mobile pantries and schools. At the same time, we help individuals and families gain long-term financial stability by providing job training, nutrition education, financial coaching, SNAP outreach, and legislative advocacy. We do this with kindness, dignity, and respect.
about:
The Food Bank of Delaware operates from its headquarters in Newark and a branch in Milford, Delaware. Founded approximately 45 years ago in a church basement, the organization has grown into a statewide network of more than 600 partner agencies.

The food bank distributes millions of pounds of food annually—including pantry staples and fresh produce from its own farms—through partner pantries, mobile pantries, school backpack programs, and direct senior deliveries. Beyond food distribution, it runs free accelerated job-training programs in warehousing/logistics and food service, and provides nutrition education, financial coaching, SNAP outreach, and legislative advocacy. The organization also operates cafes that serve the public while supporting culinary students.

Services reach food-insecure Delawareans—an estimated one in seven residents—along with adults seeking workforce credentials, seniors, children, and families. Businesses, government agencies, and other nonprofits engage as volunteers, donors, and advocacy allies.

The food bank was established to inspire hope by providing nourishment while collaborating on long-term solutions to hunger and poverty. Its stated values—compassion, respect, collaboration, empowerment, and innovation—drive a model that aims to move beyond temporary relief toward lasting financial stability for the people it serves.

name: Food Physics
old_description: systems bring positive and dramatic changes to food manufacturing
about:
Food Physics was established in 2012 in Boise, Idaho, with a second base in Chelmsford, Essex, UK. The company was founded by Kalen McKenzie, who serves as partner and CEO, to identify and maximize the potential of pulsed electric field (PEF) technology in food and beverage processing.

The company acts as the sole North American, UK, and Irish provider of PEF systems designed and built by its German partner Elea. Food Physics customizes these systems — including the Belt Advantage for solid foods, Pipe Advantage for liquids, and a PEF Pilot unit for R&D — and operates pilot halls in the United States, United Kingdom, and Germany for client-specific testing. More than 100 PEF systems have been installed worldwide, and the firm holds 17 pending PEF-related patents.

Food Physics serves food manufacturers, beverage producers, and research institutions. Its technology has been applied to potato chip and french fry production, vegetable and fruit processing, freeze drying, winemaking, and the extraction of natural dyes from spirulina (the Bequia Blue project). The company works with businesses of all sizes, from pilot-scale trials to full production lines.

The firm’s stated mission is to deliver systems that increase yield, improve product stability, and reduce waste. It differentiates itself through direct access to Elea’s R&D team, on-site engineering support, a spare-parts dispatch service, and collaborative R&D projects that drive new commercial applications.

old_description: FPWC, Inc. has operated since 1946 and is owned by Pilgrim's Pride Corporation and Cargill Meat Solutions. Since the beginning, the water cooperative has been a reliable source of
about:
Food Processors Water Cooperative, Inc. (FPWC) operates a public water supply in Timberville, Virginia, drawing from the North Fork of the Shenandoah River. Founded in 1946, the cooperative is owned by two major protein processors, Pilgrim's Pride Corporation and Cargill Meat Solutions. It began with four customers, one employee, 300,000 gallons of storage, 4,428 feet of distribution lines, and a plant rated for 500,000 gallons per day.

Today the facility employs the Roberts Filter Manhattan Process, a high-rate filtration method, across four mixed media filters that produce finished water at 1,360 gallons per minute. Treatment capacity stands at 2,000,000 gallons per day, supported by three storage tanks holding 3,300,000 gallons total. An underground distribution network of 13,239 feet serves 28 bulk-use customers, with annual sales approaching 500 million gallons. The plant runs with seven employees and certified operators who manage disinfection, coagulation, flocculation, sedimentation, and filtration, backed by on-site laboratory testing.

Primary customers include the two owner companies — both large-scale food manufacturers — as well as the Towns of Broadway and Timberville and other area businesses and residents. The cooperative's output supports food processing operations and municipal supply across the Broadway-Timberville region.

FPWC is noted as the second oldest high-rate treatment plant in Virginia. It has earned multiple Excellence in Operations awards from the Virginia Department of Health, Office of Water Programs, recognizing cross-connection control, financial management, water quality process control, distribution system management, and plant staffing and training.

Food Solutions, Inc. operates an 11,000-square-foot, USDA-, FDA- and SQF-certified food production facility and headquarters in north Denver, Colorado. Lederer serves as founder and president, with Al Bandin as vice president of culinary development.

The facility houses kettle cooking, smokehouse and sausage manufacturing equipment, a 30-by-40-foot production room, a 60-by-40-foot cook-and-raw room, a 20-by-40-foot cooler with production space, a 10-by-50-foot freezer and two drive-in docks. Services span concept development, recipe scaling, labeling design, production scheduling, fulfillment and delivery.

Food Solutions works with executive chefs and culinary directors of hotels, resorts and multi-unit restaurant operators, as well as food-service entrepreneurs and early-stage ventures. Regional and national distributors rely on the company for specialty concepts and custom culinary services. Its products are sold at Denver International Airport, education and healthcare institutions, and retail venues nationwide. Past projects include a Colorado-based quick-service sandwich chain and a Denver-based quick-service pizza brand.
